question: The base of a right prism is a triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 15 cm and 17 cm, and its lateral surface area is 480 cm². What is the volume (in cm³) of the prism?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides 8, 15, 17 form a right-angled triangle (8² + 15² = 17²).

Base Area = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm².

Base Perimeter = 8 + 15 + 17 = 40 cm.

Height of Prism = Lateral Surface Area ÷ Perimeter = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 cm.

Volume = Base Area × Height = 60 × 12 = 720 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 720 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base sides = 8 cm, 15 cm, 17 cm

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = 480 cm²

**Formula Used:**

LSA of Prism = Perimeter of base × Height

Volume of Prism = Area of base × Height

Area of right triangle = 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/546911280e55ef9f06762f18f0439944676deb3a4e47373a1df77b32e98f2789.png] 

Checking if base is a right triangle:

⇒ 8² + 15² = 64 + 225 = 289

⇒ 17² = 289

⇒ Since 8² + 15² = 17², the base is a right-angled triangle.

Calculating Base Area and Perimeter:

⇒ Area of base = 1/2 × 8 × 15 = 60 cm²

⇒ Perimeter of base = 8 + 15 + 17 = 40 cm

Finding the Height (h) of the prism:

⇒ LSA = Perimeter × h

⇒ 480 = 40 × h

⇒ h = 480 ÷ 40 = 12 cm

Calculating the Volume:

⇒ Volume = Area of base × h

⇒ Volume = 60 × 12 = 720 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 720 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Prism

The TSA is the sum of the lateral surface area and the areas of the two bases: TSA = LSA + 2 × (Area of base).

Properties of a Right Prism

In a right prism, the joining edges and faces are perpendicular to the base faces. This means the height is equal to the length of the lateral edges.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common right-triangle side ratios include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Identifying these helps in quick area and perimeter calculations.</p
